question: What is the primary focus of occupational health nursing?

options.A: Providing emergency care exclusively for motor accidents
options.C: Promoting and restoring worker health and safety
options.D: Conducting community outreach for pediatric immunizations

explanation: Occupational health nursing specifically targets the health, safety, and well-being of employed populations within their work environments. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T2#GNS225_U7_T2_h1)

question: Why is the philosophy of occupational health nursing heavily centered on prevention?

options.A: Treatment of occupational diseases is entirely impossible with modern medicine
options.B: Employers are legally forbidden from paying for medical treatments
options.C: Nurses lack the pharmacology training required to administer medications
options.D: Preventing workplace hazards stops injuries and chronic illnesses before they occur

explanation: Proactive hazard identification and control eliminate risks at the source, reducing the incidence of work-related injuries and illnesses. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T2#GNS225_U7_T2_h1)

question: Which Nigerian legislation serves as the primary legal framework for factory registration and workplace safety standards?
explanation: The Factories Act establishes baseline legal requirements for safety, machinery guarding, ventilation, and general workplace conditions in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T2#GNS225_U7_T2_h2)

question: What is the primary function of the Employees' Compensation Act administered by the NSITF?

options.A: Establishing minimum wage guidelines for government civil servants
options.B: Setting international trade tariffs for imported industrial machinery
options.C: Providing financial compensation and medical care for work-related injuries
options.D: Regulating nursing licensure and continuing education requirements

explanation: This act ensures that workers or their dependents receive financial support and medical rehabilitation when workplace injuries or occupational diseases occur. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T2#GNS225_U7_T2_h2)

question: Which category of workplace hazard includes excessive noise, vibration, and extreme temperatures?
explanation: Physical hazards involve environmental energy forces acting upon the body, such as noise, radiation, vibration, and temperature extremes. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T2#GNS225_U7_T2_h3)

question: An industrial worker who experiences chronic lower back pain due to lifting heavy loads using an awkward bending posture is exposed to which type of hazard?
explanation: Poor lifting postures and heavy manual handling strain the musculoskeletal system, classifying them directly under ergonomic hazards. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T2#GNS225_U7_T2_h3)

question: Why is Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) placed at the very bottom of the hierarchy of controls?

options.A: It relies entirely on human compliance and offers the least systemic protection
options.B: It is always the most expensive intervention for any manufacturing company
options.C: Government regulations prohibit the use of face masks and safety boots
options.D: It completely eliminates the hazard at the source before workers arrive

explanation: PPE does not remove the hazard from the environment; if worn incorrectly or damaged, the worker remains fully exposed to harm. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T2#GNS225_U7_T2_h4)

question: Installing an industrial exhaust ventilation system to remove toxic fumes from a welding workshop represents which level of control?
explanation: Engineering controls involve physical modifications to the workplace environment to isolate workers from hazards without relying on individual behavior. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T2#GNS225_U7_T2_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of a pre-placement medical examination?

options.A: To provide immediate first aid for acute industrial fractures
options.B: To establish a baseline health status and determine fitness for a specific job
options.C: To punish workers who report chronic illnesses to management
options.D: To calculate the final retirement benefits of an aging employee

explanation: Pre-placement evaluations verify that a candidate can safely perform job duties without endangering themselves or coworkers. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T2#GNS225_U7_T2_h5)

question: Which clinical activity is an occupational health nurse performing when conducting routine annual hearing tests for workers in a noisy textile mill?
explanation: Periodic screening tests monitor workers over time to detect early, subclinical indicators of occupational disease before permanent damage occurs. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T2#GNS225_U7_T2_h5)

question: What is the initial response expected from an occupational health nurse when a worker sustains an acute injury on the factory floor?

options.A: Waiting for external labor inspectors to arrive before rendering care
options.B: Filing an insurance claim with the insurance company immediately
options.C: Directing the worker to leave the premises without medical assessment
options.D: Providing immediate first aid and emergency stabilization

explanation: Immediate first aid and stabilization are vital first steps to mitigate tissue damage and prepare the patient for potential transfer. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T2#GNS225_U7_T2_h6)

question: What is the primary goal of nurse-led case management for an injured employee returning to work?

options.A: To shift all financial liability away from the employing organization
options.B: To ensure the employee is permanently demoted to a lower salary tier
options.C: To prevent the employee from ever speaking about the accident publicly
options.D: To coordinate safe rehabilitation and smooth transitional duty arrangements

explanation: Case management bridges medical recovery and workplace reentry, ensuring the worker regains productivity safely without re-injury. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T2#GNS225_U7_T2_h6)

question: Which factor is most important when designing safety education programs for a diverse industrial workforce in Nigeria?

options.A: Relying exclusively on complex medical journals written in Latin
options.B: Focusing solely on international travel medicine protocols
options.C: Using accessible language and culturally appropriate communication
options.D: Conducting training sessions only during midnight shifts

explanation: Workers can only apply safety protocols if training materials are communicated clearly in languages and formats they easily understand. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T2#GNS225_U7_T2_h7)

question: Why do occupational health nurses organize worksite programs targeting hypertension, malaria, and nutrition?

options.A: To address general lifestyle health risks that impact overall well-being and productivity
options.B: To replace government-run primary healthcare clinics in rural communities
options.C: To fulfill mandatory clinical requirements for obstetric surgical rotation
options.D: To prevent workers from ever visiting external private hospitals again

explanation: Worksite health promotion tackles systemic health issues that, while not strictly caused by the job, severely affect worker attendance and performance. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T2#GNS225_U7_T2_h7)

question: What is the primary ethical dilemma an occupational health nurse frequently faces in the workplace?

options.A: Choosing between working in a hospital ward versus an industrial factory
options.B: Balancing institutional employer loyalty with the duty of patient confidentiality and advocacy
options.C: Determining the exact market price of industrial machinery parts
options.D: Deciding whether to charge workers personal fees for first-aid supplies

explanation: Nurses are employed by management yet must prioritize worker health rights, privacy, and ethical advocacy above corporate pressures. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T2#GNS225_U7_T2_h8)

question: What should an occupational health nurse do when corporate management demands confidential medical diagnosis details of an employee without their consent?

options.A: Hand over the complete medical file immediately to satisfy superiors
options.B: Charge the employee a penalty fee for having a chronic health condition
options.C: Publish the medical records on the company notice board for transparency
options.D: Refuse disclosure to protect patient confidentiality and ethical standards

explanation: Patient confidentiality is a cornerstone of nursing ethics and professional practice, shielding medical data from unauthorized employer access. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T2#GNS225_U7_T2_h8)
